blocks.text: the people we met — who / that tushib qolganda

101-darsda **who** / **that** ta'rif ichida **ega** edi: the man **who called** me (u qo'ng'iroq qildi). Endi boshqa holat — ot ta'rif ichidagi fe'lning **to'ldiruvchisi**: the man **(who) I called** (men unga qo'ng'iroq qildim). Bunday ta'rifning o'z egasi bor (I, we, Aziz, my sister), va **who** / **that** / **which** ni tashlab yuborish mumkin: the people **we met**, the book **you gave** me. So'zlashuvda ular deyarli doim tushib qoladi.

Oddiy sinov: **who** / **that** dan keyin nima turibdi? **Fe'l** turgan bo'lsa (who **called**, that **won**) — u ega, tashlab bo'lmaydi. **Ega** (ot yoki olmosh) turgan bo'lsa (who **I** called, that **we** watched) — tashlash mumkin. Ikki gap bilan ham tekshirsa bo'ladi: We met some people. → the people (who) we met — ikkinchi gapda **people** to'ldiruvchi (we met **them**).

items.text: The coffee **you made** is too strong.
Did you find the money **you lost**?
The doctor **who examined** me was very young.
items.translation: Meni **ko'rikdan o'tkazgan** shifokor juda yosh edi.

blocks.text: O'zbekchada: [ega] + [fe'l `-gan`] + ot — «**biz uchrashgan** odamlar», «**Aziz sotib olgan** mashina». Inglizchada tartib aylanadi: ot + [ega] + [fe'l] — the people **we met**, the car **Aziz bought**. Ya'ni otni boshga olib chiqasiz, qolgan qism oddiy gapdek qoladi: we met, Aziz bought. O'zbekchada ega ba'zan egalik qo'shimchasiga aylanadi («**olgan** mashinam» = «men olgan mashina»), lekin inglizchada baribir **I** yoziladi: the car **I bought**.

items.text: I didn't like the dress **she chose**.

blocks.text: Predlog oxirida: the hotel you stayed at

Ko'p fe'llar predlog bilan ishlatiladi: stay **at**, talk **to**, listen **to**, look **for**, wait **for**, live **in**, work **for**, work **with**. Ta'rif ichida predlog fe'ldan keyin, ya'ni gap **oxirida** qoladi: We stayed **at** a hotel. → the hotel we stayed **at**. O'zbekchada esa kelishik qo'shimchasi yoki ko'makchi sifatdoshda yo'qolib ketadi: «biz **to'xtagan** mehmonxona» (`-da` yo'q), «sen **gaplashgan** qiz» («bilan» yo'q). Shuning uchun o'zbeklar ko'pincha predlogni unutadi.

items.text: The village **my mother comes from** is near Bukhara.
What's the name of the street **you live on**?

blocks.text: O'zbeklarning tipik xatolari: «the hotel we stayed» → the hotel we stayed **at** (predlog kerak!); «the book I read **it**» → the book I read (**it** ortiqcha — kitob allaqachon aytilgan); «the people we met **them**» → the people we met; «the film **what** we saw» → the film (**that**) we saw. «the hotel **at which** we stayed» ham to'g'ri, lekin juda rasmiy — so'zlashuvda: the hotel we stayed **at**.
everything, the only, the best ... I've ever ...

Ta'rif ko'pincha **everything**, **all**, **anything**, **the only**, **the first / last** va orttirma daraja (**the best**, **the most** ...) dan keyin keladi. Bu yerda ham **that** odatda tushib qoladi: everything **you said**, the only person **I trust**, the best film **I've ever seen** (→ 90-dars). **all** bu tuzilishda «faqat ..., xolos» ma'nosini beradi: All **I want** is sleep — Menga faqat uyqu kerak, xolos.

items.text: He's the nicest person **I've ever met**.

blocks.text: Eslab qolish: **who** / **that** dan keyin **ega** kelsa (I, you, we, Aziz ...) — **who** / **that** ni tashlab yuborish mumkin. Fe'l kelsa — tashlab bo'lmaydi. Predlogni (at, to, for, with, in) gap oxirida unutmang.

Bog'lanish: who / which / that ega vazifasida → 101-dars; savollarda predlog oxirida (Who are you talking **to**?) → 46-dars; fe'l + predlog (listen to, wait for) → 113-dars; the best ... I've ever ... → 90-dars.

examples.title: Object: the book (**that**) I **gave** you
examples.description: Ot ta'rif ichidagi fe'lning to'ldiruvchisi: the book **that** I **gave** you (men uni berdim). Bu yerda who / that / which bor, lekin ularni tashlab yuborish ham mumkin (ex2).

sentences.text: The cake **that** Madina **made** was delicious.
I really liked the people **who** we **met** in Bukhara.
Have you read the book **that** I **gave** you?
This is the photo **which** my brother **took** in London.
Where's the money **that** I **left** on the table?
Emma married a man **who** she **met** at university.
We didn't like the hotel **that** the travel agent **recommended**.
The shoes **which** Aziz **bought** last week are already broken.
sentences.translation: Aziz o'tgan hafta **sotib olgan** poyabzal allaqachon yirtilib qoldi.

sentences.text: Is that the song **that** you **sang** at the wedding?
My parents loved the present **which** we **sent** them from Manchester.

examples.title: Without who / that: the people **we met**
examples.description: So'zlashuvda who / that odatda tushib qoladi: ot + ega + fe'l. O'zbekcha «biz **tanishgan** odamlar» — inglizcha the people **we met**.

sentences.text: The people **we met** in Samarkand were very friendly.
Did you like the film **we watched** last night?
The questions **the teacher asked** were very easy.
I've lost the keys **you gave** me.
That's the girl **Bekzod wants** to marry.
Where are the apples **I bought** this morning?
Dilnoza showed us the dress **she's going to wear** at the wedding.
sentences.translation: Dilnoza bizga to'yda **kiymoqchi bo'lgan** ko'ylagini ko'rsatdi.

sentences.text: The soup **you made** yesterday was too salty.
Is this the coat **you want** to buy?
Tom never forgets the names of people **he meets**.
sentences.translation: Tom **tanishgan** odamlarining ismini hech qachon unutmaydi.

examples.title: Keep or leave out? **who phoned** me / **I phoned**
examples.description: Juftliklar: who / that dan keyin fe'l kelsa (ega) — tashlab bo'lmaydi; ega kelsa (to'ldiruvchi) — tashlash mumkin. O'zbekchada ikkalasi ham «`-gan`».

sentences.text: The man **who phoned** me was very polite.
sentences.translation: Menga **qo'ng'iroq qilgan** odam juda xushmuomala edi.

sentences.text: The man **I phoned** wasn't at home.
sentences.translation: Men **qo'ng'iroq qilgan** odam uyda yo'q ekan.

sentences.text: Aziz is the student **who helped** the teacher.
Aziz is the student **the teacher helped**.
I know a girl **who loves** cats.
Sarah is the girl **everybody loves**.
Where's the dog **that bit** my brother?
Where's the dog **my brother bought**?
I didn't enjoy the film **that won** the prize.
I preferred the film **we chose** ourselves.

examples.title: Preposition at the end: the hotel **we stayed at**
examples.description: Fe'l + predlog (stay at, talk to, look for, wait for, work for): ta'rifda predlog gap oxirida qoladi. O'zbekchada esa `-da`, «bilan» sifatdoshda yo'qoladi: «biz **to'xtagan** mehmonxona».

sentences.text: The hotel **we stayed at** was right next to the beach.
Who's the girl **you were talking to**?
This is the flat **I lived in** when I was a student.
I can't find the book **I was looking for**.
The music **they're listening to** is too loud.
Bekzod got the job **he applied for**!
Is that the bus **we're waiting for**?
Manchester is the city **my father was born in**.
The company **Madina works for** is opening an office in London.
Those are the friends **Aziz plays football with** every Sunday.
sentences.translation: Ular — Aziz har yakshanba **birga futbol o'ynaydigan** do'stlari.

examples.title: More prepositions: **with**, **about**, **on**, **of**
examples.description: Boshqa predloglar ham oxirida qoladi: work **with**, tell **about**, sit **on**, be afraid **of**, be proud **of**, ask **for**, speak **to**.

sentences.text: These are the colleagues **I work with**.
Is this the problem **you told me about**?
The man **Sarah is married to** is a famous chef.
We visited the village **my grandmother grew up in**.
That's the topic **we argued about** all evening.
The chair **you're sitting on** is broken.
Do you remember the teacher **we were all afraid of**?
Here's the address **you asked for**.
James showed me the photos **he was so proud of**.
The man **I spoke to** on the phone gave me the wrong information.
sentences.translation: Telefonda **gaplashgan** odamim menga noto'g'ri ma'lumot berdi.

examples.title: Questions: Is this the umbrella **you lost**?
examples.description: Savol-javob: savollarda ham ta'rif otdan keyin keladi, who / that ko'pincha tushib qoladi.

sentences.text: Is this the umbrella **you lost**? — Yes, it's mine!
What's the name of the restaurant **we went to** last year? — I think it was Afsona.
sentences.translation: O'tgan yili **borgan** restoranimizning nomi nima edi? — Menimcha, «Afsona».

sentences.text: Did you like the presents **we bought** for the children? — Yes, they were perfect.
sentences.translation: Bolalarga **olgan** sovg'alarimiz yoqdimi? — Ha, juda zo'r ekan.

sentences.text: Who was the man **you were with** at the cinema? — My cousin from Bukhara.
sentences.translation: Kinoteatrda **birga bo'lgan** odaming kim edi? — Buxorolik amakivachcham.

sentences.text: Where's the jacket **I lent you**? — It's in my car.
Are these the shoes **you want**? — No, the ones **I want** are black.
Have you seen the email **the manager sent** this morning? — Not yet.
sentences.translation: Bugun ertalab menejer **yuborgan** xatni ko'rdingmi? — Hali yo'q.

sentences.text: How was the hotel **you stayed at** in London? — Small but comfortable.
sentences.translation: Londonda **to'xtagan** mehmonxonang qanaqa edi? — Kichik, lekin qulay.

sentences.text: Can I borrow the novel **you finished** last week? — Of course, here it is.
sentences.translation: O'tgan hafta **o'qib tugatgan** romaningni olib tursam bo'ladimi? — Albatta, mana.

sentences.text: What did you think of the guide **we had** in Samarkand? — He was brilliant.
sentences.translation: Samarqandda **bizga hamroh bo'lgan** gid sizga qanday tuyuldi? — Zo'r edi.

examples.title: everything / the only / the best ... **I've ever** ...
examples.description: **everything**, **all**, **the only**, **the first** va orttirma daraja (the best ...) dan keyin that odatda tushib qoladi: the best plov **I've ever eaten**.

sentences.text: This is the best plov **I've ever eaten**.
sentences.translation: Bu men umrimda **yegan** eng mazali palov.

sentences.text: Everything **you told me** was true.
Sarah is the only person **I trust** completely.
It was the most boring lesson **we've ever had**.
sentences.translation: Bu bizda **bo'lgan** eng zerikarli dars edi.

sentences.text: Is there anything **you need** from the shop?
Samarkand is the most beautiful city **I've ever visited**.
That was the last thing **I expected**!
All **I want** is a cup of hot tea.
sentences.translation: Menga faqat bir piyola issiq choy **kerak**, xolos.

sentences.text: The first thing **Bekzod does** in the morning is check his phone.
sentences.translation: Bekzod ertalab **qiladigan** birinchi ish — telefonini tekshirish.

sentences.text: Emma is the funniest person **I know**.

examples.title: Dialogue: back from a trip
examples.description: Safardan qaytgan do'st bilan suhbat: the hotel **we stayed at**, the people **we met**, the photos **you took**.

sentences.text: — How was the trip? Did you like the places **you visited**?
— Yes! The hotel **we stayed at** in Bukhara was wonderful.
— Is that the hotel **your sister recommended**?
— Yes, it is. And the people **we met** there were really kind.
sentences.translation: — Ha, o'sha. U yerda **tanishgan** odamlarimiz ham juda mehribon edi.

sentences.text: — What about the food? Was it as good as the food **you eat** at home?
— Even better! The plov **they cooked** for us was amazing.
sentences.translation: — Undan ham zo'r! Ular bizga **pishirgan** palov ajoyib edi.

sentences.text: — Did you buy the carpet **you were talking about**?
— No. The one **I wanted** was too expensive.
— Shame. Can I see the photos **you took**?
— Of course. These are the ones **I like** most.
